A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StaR-KVQA, with matching core components, datasets, and main experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, including v1's appendix and image-based prompts. The supplied v2 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original OK-VQA and FVQA experiments, component ablations, candidate-count sensitivity, cross-domain transfer, and generated qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark, ablation, transfer, and qualitative results, and adds evaluated CoT + SFT baseline results.

M1.justification: The planner, composer, same-model selector, training objective, and single-pass inference remain. However, v2 Section 4.2 explicitly rejects low-coverage explanations before selection, whereas v1 describes path binding and theoretical coverage constraints without this operational step. The PDFs do not establish whether filtering is newly introduced or newly documented.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on OK-VQA and FVQA and test transfer in both directions. Revised qualitative examples remain within this coverage; no additional dataset, domain, or distinct evaluation scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Qwen2.5-VL-7B CoT + SFT comparator to Tables 1 and 2. In the retained ship and sofa case studies, it removes Qwen and Llama baseline responses while retaining Gemma-3-12B and Gemini 2.5 Pro. Other quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve the reported backbones, training hyperparameters, dataset-specific K values, default decoding, and normalized direct-answer VQA metric. v2 clarifies exceptions for explicitly specified CoT baselines. Its vLLM timing context is newly disclosed information, without an established before-and-after protocol change.

E4.justification: Component ablations, K sensitivity, and cross-domain analyses remain. Qualitative analysis contracts from five examples in v1 Tables 5–9 to revised ship and sofa examples in v2 Tables 5–6, removing the venue, wind-strength, and Canadian-location cases and reducing backbone-specific evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 and single-run reporting. Neither reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v2 condenses the existing disclosure rather than introducing a different statistical practice.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy entries in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged, while CoT + SFT adds 79.58% on OK-VQA and 75.13% on FVQA. Figure 3 substantially revises construction times from approximately 9–44 seconds to 0.5–2.2 seconds per example. Several qualitative outputs are removed or replaced with different traces. The timing revision is not an established same-setting speedup because comparable execution conditions are not documented.

T1.justification: v2 removes all of v1 Appendix A.3: trace-feasibility definitions, the Rademacher-complexity claim, selector MLE/MAP analysis, KL-based self-distillation results, and the likelihood-bound derivation and proofs. The main task and method equations remain.

C1.justification: The central reasoning claim is substantively narrowed. v1 presents structured traces as faithful, verifiable reasoning; v2 emphasizes transparent intermediate behavior and modality-aware soft scaffolds, explicitly disclaiming guaranteed faithfulness. The single-model, retrieval-free contribution and reported accuracy advantage remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly allows redundant or spurious path hops, additional composer cues, and answer-oriented selection that may produce unintuitive or unfaithful explanations. Its conclusion acknowledges path–explanation mismatches beyond v1's existing hallucination caveat. It also adds an interpretation of the revised timings as supporting practical deployment.

D1.justification: Most training settings move from v1 Appendix A.1.1 into v2 Section 5.1. However, v2 removes all three exact prompt templates, path-serialization instructions, and details such as the selector's ground-truth input and Gemini Dynamic Thinking mode. It adds coverage-filtering instructions and vLLM/L20-server information, leaving substantially different reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage is largely retained. Mikolov et al. (2013) disappears with the discussion rejecting Word2Vec-based scoring. Positioning more explicitly contrasts modality-aware structured scaffolds with generic chain-of-thought supervision, without a substantial expansion of cited research.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and conclusion, changes the title, removes the research-question organization, and condenses baseline, implementation, and metric material into Section 5.1. The appendix structure is removed, with selected content incorporated into the main text.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column presentation. Figure 2's example paths and caption are revised, Figure 3's time axes change, ablation rows receive descriptive names, and cross-domain deltas gain color coding. Three prompt figures and three case-study tables disappear; the two retained cases are condensed and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added CoT + SFT control and explicit faithfulness limitations improve comparison and claim calibration. However, removing exact prompts and serialization details weakens reproducibility, while the substantially revised timings and replacement case-study traces lack enough provenance to assess their evidential quality. With main accuracy results unchanged, these benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
